styles.label: Ancient
styles.blurb: Colosseum, Forum and Pantheon in the open-air museum of the centre.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Vatican Museums, Borghese Gallery and churches full of Caravaggio.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Cacio e pepe, supplì and long lunches in Trastevere.

stays.why: Walk to the Pantheon, Piazza Navona and the Trevi Fountain. Best for a first visit with little time.
Cobbled lanes and dinner spots across the river. Lively at night, quieter by day.
Small streets next to the Colosseum and Forum. Good mix of cafés, bars and local feel.
Close to St Peter's and the Vatican Museums. Calmer streets and good metro links.

food: Order Roman classics: cacio e pepe, carbonara, amatriciana and saltimbocca. Portions are big; a primo is often enough.
Pizza al taglio is sold by weight at counters. Point at what you want; pay about €3–6 for a good slice.
Coffee standing at the bar costs far less than sitting at a table. Cappuccino is a morning drink for locals.
Book dinner in Trastevere or Testaccio for a lively night. Many kitchens close mid-afternoon; eat lunch around 13:00.
Try a supplì (fried rice ball) and a scoop of gelato from a shop that keeps it covered, not piled high.
more_time: Swap a half-day for Ostia Antica: train from Piramide, about 30 minutes, to Roman ruins without the crowds.
Add a day trip to Tivoli for Villa d'Este gardens and Hadrian's Villa; trains and buses run from the city.
Art lovers can swap a museum morning for the Borghese Gallery; timed tickets sell out, so book ahead.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the Colosseum and Forum, the Vatican Museums and a relaxed evening in Trastevere without rushing.

month_notes: January: cold and quiet, highs near 12°C. Pack a warm coat and expect some rain.
February: still cool at 14°C highs, fewer crowds. Good for museums.
March: mild at 16°C but one of the wetter months. Carry an umbrella.
April: pleasant 20°C days, busy with spring crowds. Book sights ahead.
May: warm at 23°C with some showers. Great for walking the centre.
June: hot at 29°C and dry. Sightsee early morning and late afternoon.
July: very hot, 33°C highs. Use midday for churches and museums.
August: as hot as July and many local shops close. Some restaurants shut for holidays.
September: warm at 27°C and drier. One of the best months to visit.
October: mild at 22°C but rain picks up. Layer up.
November: cooler at 17°C and the wettest month. Indoor plans help.
December: cold at 14°C highs with rain. Festive lights and nativity scenes.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean climate: hot, dry summers and mild, wetter winters. Spring and autumn are the sweet spots.

items.title: Best months: April–May and September–October
items.text: Highs of 20–27°C with manageable rain. Ideal for walking between sights.

items.title: Summer is hot and dry
items.text: July and August hit 33°C with only 4–5 rain days. Plan outdoor sights for early morning.

items.title: Wettest in autumn and early spring
items.text: November has about 13 rain days, March 11. Showers are often short; carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Winter is cool, not freezing
items.text: January highs near 12°C and lows around 4°C. A warm coat and layers are enough.

items.title: Wear good shoes
items.text: Cobblestones and long museum days mean a lot of walking in any season.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light layers in spring and autumn, sun hat and water bottle in summer, warm coat and umbrella in winter. Cover shoulders and knees for churches.

transit.best: Walk the centre; use the metro and buses for longer hops and taxis for late nights.

modes.text: Two main lines (A and B) plus a short branch. Useful but limited coverage; good for the Vatican and Colosseum areas.
Trams and city buses fill the gaps. Buy tickets before boarding.
Taxis use fixed airport fares and meters in town. Uber works in Rome.
Driving in the centre is chaotic and ZTL cameras fine you. Don't do it.
The best way to see the centre. Bikes and scooters are common.
No ferry needed in the city; cruise ships dock at Civitavecchia, reached by train.
